findings.finding: Interior's 2025 M-25-21 AI Compliance Plan commits the Department to ensure all employees whose work could benefit from AI models have access to such tools, but states no seat count and does not name a 'DOI ChatGPT' tool.
findings.exact_quote: The Department will coordinate with the CAIO Council to leverage government-wide training programs, participate in federal staff talent-exchange programs, and ensure all employees whose work could benefit from AI models have access to such tools.
findings.source_title: Department of the Interior Artificial Intelligence Compliance Plan (OMB M-25-21) - U.S. Department of the Interior
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full 12-page PDF, with two corrections: (1) the original exact_quote was a truncated fragment ('employees whose work could benefit from AI models have access to such tools.'); the verbatim sentence in the plan's Workforce Development section is longer and is now quoted in full. (2) The original finding claimed the plan 'confirms the Department provides a security-controlled commercial LLM called DOI ChatGPT' — this is NOT supported: the string 'DOI ChatGPT' does not appear anywhere in the 2025 compliance plan. The 'DOI ChatGPT' name reportedly comes from a separate/earlier (2024) DOI document, not this source; finding text corrected to remove the unsupported attribution. The 2025 plan reaffirms the AI Action Plan mandate but gives no number of users or licenses. The OMB 2025 inventory's '50,000+' figure attaches to Microsoft Copilot/Copilot Chat and Synthesia for written communications; against a ~70,000 workforce that implies near-agency-wide availability, but no public press release corroborates the 50,000 figure. Coverage marked unknown because the public record does not independently confirm scale.

findings.finding: OMB's 2025 inventory reports DOI Microsoft Copilot/Copilot Chat plus Synthesia at 50,000+ users for written communications; no public press release independently corroborates that figure.
findings.notes: Searched FedScoop, Nextgov/FCW, GovExec, MeriTalk and DOI.gov for a Copilot rollout announcement at Interior; none surfaced. The 50,000+ figure rests solely on the agency's self-reported OMB inventory entry. Against a ~70,000 workforce that would be 'most' employees, consistent with the government-wide Microsoft 365 Copilot OneGov offer (free for G5 customers), but this is a license-availability count, not a verified active-user count.

findings.finding: DOT's Volpe Center built and launched the department's first employee-facing AI chatbot, chat.dot.gov, reaching more than 5,000 users as a technology demonstrator.
findings.exact_quote: The chat.dot.gov platform served as a successful AI technology demonstrator ... ultimately reached a user base of more than 5,000 users and averaged 900 simultaneous active users daily.
findings.source_title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence at U.S. Department of Transportation - Volpe National Transportation Systems Center
findings.notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED: the volpe.dot.gov page is bot-blocked (HTTP 403 on two direct fetch attempts, incl. a Google-cache attempt). A WebSearch of the same URL confirms the page exists and corroborates the substance — 'served as a successful AI technology demonstrator', 'reached a user base of more than 5,000 users', 'averaged 900 simultaneous active users daily'. However the exact verbatim wording of the FULL sentence could NOT be confirmed against the live page: the search rendering shows 'ultimately reached a user base' (not 'ultimately reaching a user base') and does NOT contain the trailing 'while maintaining nearly 100% uptime' clause that the original quote included. exact_quote downgraded to the elided, search-corroborated form; the 5,000+ users and 900-simultaneous figures are corroborated, the 'nearly 100% uptime' clause is UNVERIFIED and was dropped. VERIFY: re-fetch the live volpe.dot.gov page to restore an exact full-sentence quote if needed. The 5,000+ user figure aligns with the OMB inventory's 'Azure AI Foundry' 1,001-5,000 band and the internal 'Enterprise Personal Productivity Assistant'. Against a ~55,000 DOT workforce, 5,000 users is a partial/pilot-scale deployment, explicitly framed as a 'technology demonstrator' rather than agency-wide rollout. The inventory also notes an 'Ask Dottie' chatbot and a DOT-wide generative AI policy; 'Ask Dottie' did not surface in any public search.

findings.tool_name: DOT generative AI program (Gemini / regulation drafting)
findings.finding: DOT has a publicly reported department-wide generative AI effort and plans to use Google Gemini to help draft regulations, but no public source gives a general-purpose chat-tool seat count beyond chat.dot.gov.
findings.source_title: U.S. DOT Artificial Intelligence Activities - US Department of Transportation
findings.notes: ProPublica, Undark and Global Government Forum covered DOT's plan to use AI (Google Gemini) to draft transportation regulations, and DOT published an AI Strategy Part III Compliance Plan. These confirm a DOT-wide generative-AI policy exists but describe a task-specific drafting use, not a general-purpose chat assistant with a disclosed user count. No commercial general-purpose chat tool seat count beyond chat.dot.gov's 5,000+ was found.

findings.finding: Federal contract records show the IRS purchased 150 ChatGPT Enterprise licenses for use within the Treasury Department; Treasury later tested ChatGPT among a limited user group, with reporting of a subsequent move toward up to 3,000 licenses.
findings.estimated_users: 150 licenses initially; reporting of up to 3,000 licenses subsequently
findings.exact_quote: the Internal Revenue Service purchased 150 ChatGPT Enterprise Licenses for use within the Department of the Treasury through a federal contractor, though it's not clear how many were or have been used.
findings.source_title: OpenAI further expands its generative AI work with the federal government - FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries the quote verbatim (full page sentence: 'Earlier this fall, the Internal Revenue Service purchased 150 ChatGPT Enterprise Licenses for use within the Department of the Treasury through a federal contractor, though it's not clear how many were or have been used.'). This finding sharply contradicts and clarifies the OMB inventory field: the 2025 inventory reports 5,001-10,000 Treasury users for drafting/writing but named NO commercial product (field left 'N/A'). The public record shows the actual named commercial general-purpose tool is ChatGPT Enterprise, but verified procurement is only 150 licenses (FedScoop, Nov 2024) - far below the 5,001-10,000 band. Separate reporting (a DOGE-affiliated Treasury CIO approving ~$1.5M for up to 3,000 ChatGPT licenses) suggests later expansion but is still well under the inventory band and was not fetched to verbatim here. The inventory's 5,001-10,000 likely reflects M365 Copilot Chat availability across Treasury's ~100,000 (mostly IRS) workforce rather than ChatGPT seats. Best public characterization: a pilot/limited-deployment posture for named commercial general-purpose AI as of late 2024-2025.

findings.finding: State's internally built enterprise GenAI chatbot StateChat, launched August 2024, grew from 3,000 beta testers to 45,000-50,000 users out of an ~80,000-person workforce by September 2025.
findings.exact_quote: The department initially rolled out its chatbot to 3,000 beta testers. Now it is being used by 45,000 to 50,000 people out of the department's 80,000-strong workforce
findings.source_title: State Department hopes to use agentic AI to assist employee tasks, CIO says - Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: Nextgov carries the quoted text verbatim. StateChat is a documented, deliberate department-wide rollout (not merely 'technically available') - State built it on Palantir + Azure OpenAI, approved for Sensitive But Unclassified data, and made it available to all 75,000+ State personnel worldwide. CIO Kelly Fletcher gave the 45,000-50,000 cumulative-user figure in September 2025. Against a ~80,000 workforce this is 'most' employees having used it. Strongly corroborates the OMB inventory's 5,001-10,000 figure as a conservative weekly-active count rather than total reach. Multiple outlets (FedScoop, Federal News Network, Nextgov) independently confirm the program.

findings.finding: StateChat averaged about 10,000 weekly users in spring 2025 and roughly 20,000 weekly users by March 2026, having amassed roughly 3 million prompts.
findings.source_title: Mobile app, cable queries among planned expansions of State Department's AI chatbot - FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries 'averages about 10,000 users a week' verbatim (full sentence: 'According to Silson, since that launch, the tool has amassed roughly 3 million prompts in its system and averages about 10,000 users a week.'). This finding distinguishes weekly active users (~10,000 in 2025, ~20,000 by March 2026 per Federal News Network) from the 45,000-50,000 cumulative-users figure. The OMB inventory's 5,001-10,000 band aligns closely with the ~10,000 weekly-active count at the time the inventory was filed. State estimates StateChat saves 20,000-30,000 hours per week. The Federal News Network March 2026 article that reports ~20,000 weekly users returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so the 2026 weekly figure is from a search excerpt; the 2025 ~10,000 figure is verbatim from the fetched FedScoop article.

findings.finding: NASA published a December 2025 Privacy Impact Assessment for Microsoft Copilot, confirming NASA licenses Microsoft 365 Copilot (plus free Copilot Chat) as a digital assistant for government employees, but the PIA discloses no user count.
findings.exact_quote: Copilot for M365 is a licensed AI-powered tool for use as a digital assistant.
findings.source_title: National Aeronautics and Space Administration Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA): Microsoft Copilot - NASA
findings.notes: The PIA confirms NASA has authorized Microsoft 365 Copilot agency-wide for 'Government Employees' and 'NASA Contractors' and that the free-tier Copilot Chat (M365 Copilot Light) is available. It is an agency-wide authorization document, not a center-specific tool, but it gives no seat/license count, so scale is unknown. The OMB 2025 inventory reports Microsoft Copilot + Gemini at 1,001-5,000 users; against NASA's ~18,000 workforce that 1,001-5,000 band implies partial-to-moderate active use even though the PIA authorizes Copilot broadly. Treated as 'technically available agency-wide' with unknown deliberate active-rollout scale.

findings.finding: NASA ran center-specific generative-AI chatbots - a Goddard pilot for document editing and code explanation and a Langley chatbot for processing controlled unclassified information, both on Claude Sonnet 3.5 - but no public source names 'ALTIRA' or gives user counts.
findings.exact_quote: a pilot chatbot to assist Goddard Space Flight Center employees with tasks like document editing and explaining code
findings.source_title: NASA chatbots, Treasury coding, OPM drafting: How agencies have deployed Claude - FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED against full page: FedScoop carries the quote 'a pilot chatbot to assist Goddard Space Flight Center employees with tasks like document editing and explaining code' verbatim. The OMB inventory names an internal NASA chatbot 'ALTIRA' (Accelerated Langley Transformation Initiative Research Assistant) - a single-center (Langley) tool, NOT agency-wide. Extensive searches of nasa.gov, larc.nasa.gov, FedScoop and Nextgov returned no public mention of 'ALTIRA' by name; the closest corroboration is FedScoop's report of a Langley Claude-based chatbot for controlled unclassified information plus a separate Goddard pilot. These are explicitly center-level pilots, not an agency-wide general-purpose deployment, and no user counts are public. The 'ALTIRA' name appears to be inventory-only with no public footprint.
